capabilities: Import classical Arabic texts from curated public repositories as linked notes
Transcribe scanned PDFs via Gemini OCR and translate the transcriptions
Transliterate Arabic passages through a local CAMeL-based server
Annotate imported sources with annotations stored separately from generated notes
Export imported works as auto-updated Zotero items
extras: Desktop only; runs local Python scripts and reads and writes files outside the vault, including absolute paths. Full documentation is bundled in-app via an Open documentation command. The plugin was submitted for community review at the time of writing, so BRAT installation is offered as an alternative. No fonts are downloaded; it relies on locally installed Arabic and Latin typefaces with documented fallback chains. Collects no telemetry.
motivation: The author built it for research on Islam and the Arabic language — Qurʾān commentaries, ḥadīth, the Qurʾān in its riwāyāt, and the classical dictionaries.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to bring digitized Arabic corpora and scanned Arabic PDFs into the vault as searchable, annotatable, linkable notes, or to romanize Arabic for English writing.

relations.evidence: Midad Arabic Sources’ ETA templating, managed-region merge, and note conventions follow ScholarWeft
Zotero (optional) for sending imported works to your library.
normally created by ScholarWeft or ZotLit; Midad does not create those notes

requires.name: Python 3 with PyMuPDF, requests, and CAMeL Tools

summary: Research toolkit that imports classical Arabic sources, OCRs scanned PDFs, transliterates Arabic, and exports references to Zotero.
